label: Dreischulte 44
title: Warfarin with a tetracycline antibiotic
statement: Patient treated with warfarin - is co-prescribed tetracyclines

plain_summary: A supply of a tetracycline antibiotic during warfarin treatment calls for a review of the interaction and the patient's INR monitoring.

medicine_groups.name: Warfarin
medicine_groups.note: Use the dated supply and the current anticoagulation directions.

medicine_groups.name: A tetracycline antibiotic
medicine_groups.note: Count systemic tetracycline antibiotics. The strength and length of the course do not determine whether the pair is present.

rule_for_models: In a patient taking Group A warfarin, suspect a finding when Group A and Group B (a tetracycline antibiotic) supply dates overlap or fall within 60 days of each other and the intended courses can overlap. Calculate the last treatment day from the form, start date, directions, quantity and any hold or stop, and give no finding if one course ended before the other began, even when supply dates are within 60 days. Cite both supplies even if there is no INR result. When the supplies are within 60 days and unclear directions leave overlap uncertain, cite both supplies and report only a possible finding. Ask the pharmacist to confirm the dose actually used and the treatment dates. A documented stop, hold or later start that rules out overlap gives no finding.
cannot_be_seen: The supplies alone cannot show whether both medicines were taken, how the INR changed, whether bleeding occurred or what monitoring was arranged elsewhere.
ask_the_gp: Could you review this tetracycline course alongside the patient's INR results and monitoring plan?
